It supports activities aimed at increasing knowledge, understanding, action, and response in order to strengthen, enhance and maintain water sustainability.
WWA partners with local, regional and national governments to support WWA’s work to address climate change; the WWA is committed to supporting countries and local communities to address water challenges, including those that are associated with climate change, such as droughts, floods, and heat waves. In addition, WWA seeks to ensure that WWA develops and implements policies that promote safe drinking water supplies.
In 2015, WWA launched its Global Environment Facility (GEF) which aims to achieve climate action goals by 2030.

Get a head start on your health.
During this time of year, it is important to take care of yourself and to be sure that you are eating a balanced diet. Eating a well-balanced diet can help you stay healthy through all aspects of your life, including physical activity and nutrition. Here are some tips for staying healthy throughout the winter months.
Try to eat a variety of foods from each food group. Choose fruits and vegetables when possible. This will keep your body full and allows your body to recover after a hard workout. Also, make sure that you have enough fiber in your meals. You should also try to avoid processed food like packaged ready meals or frozen meal. If you don’t do these things regularly, your body may become accustomed to eating less fat and sugar than it used to. It’s important to limit your intake of carbohydrates (white bread, pasta, rice) and fats (brass, butter, cheese). These could cause blood sugar levels to rise and your weight to drop. Try to get more whole grains in your meals rather than refined ones. Look for whole grain breads, cereals, crackers, pastas and cereal bars instead. These are low in sugar but high in fat. They have been shown to decrease insulin levels.

At CUP, we are trying to understand how corals work as they live and what it is like in these waters. Our goal is to help scientists learn about corals and how they respond to climate change.
What is coral reef? A coral reef is a structure made up of layers of rock, coral skeletons and other living organisms that shelter the reef floor. The surface of a coral reef is typically covered by many different types of algae called zooxanthellae, which create a protective shell on top of the underlying material. This keeps the sea level low enough so that water can flow freely through the reef and its inhabitants. Some of the most important processes within the reef are photosynthesis, photochemistry and respiration.
How does a coral reef work? The main function of a coral reef is to support an animal and plant life. These include fish, insects, corals, and plants. The type of algae present at each site determines whether or not a reef will be closed off.
